description: Investigating computer crime by the book: identifying, acquiring, preserving, analysing and presenting digital evidence from disks, memory, mobile devices and networks in a way that survives a courtroom. Taught to the depth of a leading digital forensics course and the professional examiner certifications.
modelledOn: Nelson, Phillips and Steuart, Guide to Computer Forensics and Investigations
Casey, Digital Evidence and Computer Crime
NIST SP 800-86 Guide to Integrating Forensic Techniques into Incident Response
SANS GIAC Certified Forensic Examiner (GCFE) objectives
outcomes: Explain the forensic process and the legal framework for digital evidence in Ghana and internationally.
Acquire forensically sound images of disks, memory and mobile devices and verify them with hashes.
Analyse file systems, deleted data, metadata, logs and artefacts of Windows, Linux and Android.
Recover and interpret evidence from email, web, network captures and cloud services.
Build a case file with a chain of custody and write an expert report.
Describe the responsibilities and liabilities of an investigator and testify as an expert witness.

units.title: Introduction to computer forensics
topics: Digital forensics as a discipline: history, branches (computer, network, mobile, memory, cloud), and its relation to incident response
The forensic process: identification, preservation, collection, examination, analysis, presentation
Locard's exchange principle in the digital world; the examiner's mindset
Setting up a forensic workstation and lab with open-source tools (Autopsy, Sleuth Kit, FTK Imager, Volatility, Wireshark)

units.title: Computer crimes and criminals
topics: Categories of computer crime: fraud, sakawa and romance scams, mobile-money fraud, intrusion, malware, harassment, child abuse material, intellectual property theft
Offender profiles and motives; insider threats
Ghana's Cybersecurity Act 2020 and Electronic Transactions Act 2008; the Budapest Convention; cross-border cooperation
Roles: law enforcement (Cyber Security Authority, CID), corporate investigators, private examiners

units.title: Forensic technologies and tools
topics: Write blockers, imaging hardware, Faraday bags, evidence storage
Commercial and open-source suites; validating tools; NIST tool testing
Hashing (MD5, SHA-256) and why it proves integrity; hash sets and known-file filtering
Virtual machines and sandboxes for safe examination

units.title: Computer hardware and software in forensics
topics: Storage media: HDD geometry, SSDs and TRIM, flash, optical, RAID; where data hides (slack space, unallocated space, HPA/DCO)
Boot process, BIOS/UEFI, partitions (MBR, GPT)
File systems: FAT, NTFS (MFT, ADS, journal), ext4, APFS; timestamps and their interpretation
Operating system artefacts: registry, event logs, prefetch, LNK files, shellbags, user profiles
Encryption and anti-forensics: BitLocker, VeraCrypt, wiping, steganography

units.title: Collecting and preserving digital evidence
topics: First response: securing the scene, photographing, documenting, deciding on live versus dead acquisition
Volatile data collection: RAM imaging, running processes, network connections; order of volatility
Disk imaging: bit-for-bit copies, E01 and raw formats, verification; imaging phones and cloud accounts
Chain of custody forms, evidence bags, labelling, storage; legal authority and warrants
Handling evidence from mobile money, social media and messaging apps

units.title: Preserving and recovering digital evidence
topics: File carving by signatures; recovering deleted files from FAT and NTFS; recycle bin analysis
Timeline analysis with the Sleuth Kit and Plaso; super-timelines
Memory forensics with Volatility: processes, injected code, passwords, network artefacts
Email forensics: headers, spoofing, PST/MBOX analysis; web browser artefacts: history, cache, cookies
Mobile forensics: Android and iOS logical and physical acquisition, SQLite databases, app data
Network forensics: packet captures, flow records, log correlation; cloud and IoT evidence

units.title: Building a cybercrime case
topics: Case planning: hypotheses, scope, evidence sources, legal constraints
Keyword and pattern searching, data reduction, filtering known files, linking artefacts to users and times
Attribution: user accounts, device identifiers, IP addresses, geolocation and their limits
Writing the forensic report: findings, methodology, reproducibility, exhibits
Case exercise: a fraud investigation from seized laptop to report

units.title: Investigator responsibilities and liabilities
topics: Admissibility of digital evidence: authenticity, integrity, relevance, hearsay; Ghana's Evidence Act and electronic evidence provisions
Expert witness duties, testimony, cross-examination; courtroom presentation of technical material
Privacy, proportionality and data protection during investigations; handling illegal material
Professional ethics and codes (ISFCE, ACPO principles); liabilities for negligence, contamination and disclosure

units.title: Corporate investigations and incident response
topics: Investigations inside organisations: policy, HR, legal and IT cooperation; acceptable use policies
Incident response life cycle and where forensics fits; preserving evidence during containment
E-discovery and litigation holds
Capstone: full investigation of a prepared disk image with report and mock testimony

schedule.title: The discipline and the forensic process
schedule.exercise: Write a one-page comparison of the six stages of the forensic process, giving one example of what goes wrong at each stage when it is skipped.

tasks.title: Put the six forensic process stages in order for a stolen-laptop case and justify each decision from the evidence listed in the scenario
Examine a prepared virtual machine to find five traces a user left behind, linking each to Locard's principle in a short note
Set up a forensic workstation image with a hash tool and a read-only mount, then document the set-up so another examiner can reproduce it

schedule.title: Computer crime, offenders and law
schedule.exercise: Short essay: choose one mobile-money fraud pattern and map its offender motive, the law that applies and the agency that would investigate.

tasks.title: Classify eight reported incidents, including a romance scam and a SIM-swap fraud, into crime categories and name the key evidence source for each
Work a case with a cross-border suspect and decide which Cybersecurity Act or Budapest Convention steps apply, scored against a rubric
Investigate a suspected insider leak at a company, rank suspects by access and motive from the evidence, and justify what you would not conclude

schedule.title: Tools, hashing and safe examination
schedule.exercise: Explain in writing why a matching SHA-256 value proves integrity but not authenticity, and when MD5 is still acceptable in a lab.

tasks.title: Hash a file with MD5 and SHA-256 in the shell, change one byte, hash again, and record both values to show integrity checking
Build a known-file hash set from a clean directory, then filter a suspect directory to list only the files not in the set
Detonate a suspicious sample in an isolated virtual machine, record the files and processes it creates, and write the containment steps you used

schedule.title: Storage, boot and file systems
schedule.exercise: Draw a labelled map of an MBR disk with two partitions showing where slack space and unallocated space can hold hidden data.

tasks.title: Read the partition table of a disk image, list each partition's type and start sector, and identify whether it uses MBR or GPT
Compare the timestamps of a file before and after copying, moving and editing it on a simulated NTFS volume and explain each change
Find data hidden in slack space, unallocated space and an alternate data stream of a prepared image, and document where each item sits

schedule.title: Operating system artefacts and anti-forensics
schedule.exercise: Write a short note listing the Windows artefacts that would show a USB drive was plugged in, with the question each artefact answers.

tasks.title: Open a prepared event log and list every logon event for one user on a given day, noting time, type and source
Combine registry, prefetch and shellbag entries from an image to prove which program opened a document and when
Investigate a suspect machine with an encrypted volume and a wiping tool, decide lawful next steps, and justify what can and cannot be proved

schedule.title: First response and acquisition
schedule.exercise: Draw up a first-response checklist for a small business office raided after a fraud report, with the reason for each item.

tasks.title: Order eight volatile and non-volatile data sources by volatility for a running laptop and justify what to capture first
Create a bit-for-bit image of a virtual disk, hash the source and the image, and confirm the two values match
Handle a live-versus-dead acquisition scenario at a cyber cafe, choosing actions at each decision point and being scored on evidence preserved

schedule.title: Chain of custody and mobile money evidence
schedule.exercise: Fill in a complete chain-of-custody form for three items seized in a mobile-money fraud case, including every hand-over and storage location.

tasks.title: Complete a chain-of-custody form for a seized phone and laptop, then spot the gaps a defence lawyer would attack in a sample form
Review a mobile-money statement and chat export from a fraud case and identify the transactions and messages that link the suspect to the victim
Decide, within a warrant's limits, what a team may seize and search in a mixed home and office raid, and defend each decision

schedule.title: Carving, timelines and memory
schedule.exercise: Prepare a short method statement describing how you would validate a file-carving result before trusting it in a report.

tasks.title: Recover three deleted files from a prepared disk image by their header signatures and verify each opens correctly
Build a timeline of a prepared image from file times and logs, and find the window in which the suspect activity occurred
Analyse a memory dump to find a hidden process, the network connection it holds and an injected code region, then report the evidence

schedule.title: Email, mobile and network forensics
schedule.exercise: Write up how you would tell a spoofed email from a genuine one by reading its headers, using two examples side by side.

tasks.title: Read the full headers of a phishing email, trace the sending path hop by hop, and mark the line that exposes the spoofing
Query the SQLite message database from a phone image to list all messages between two numbers in a one-week window
Correlate a packet capture, router logs and a web server log to reconstruct how data left the network, with a timeline of events

schedule.title: Case planning and attribution
schedule.exercise: Draft an investigation plan for a case of payroll fraud, stating hypotheses, data sources, legal limits and what would disprove each hypothesis.

tasks.title: Write three hypotheses and the evidence sources for each in a payroll fraud case, then rank them by how testable they are
Search a prepared image with keywords and patterns, filter out known files, and reduce thousands of files to the few relevant to the case
Assess an attribution claim that rests on an IP address and a shared account, and write what the evidence supports and what it cannot

schedule.title: Reporting and the case exercise
schedule.exercise: Write a two-page report extract giving findings, methods and exhibits for the fraud case so that a second examiner could repeat every step.

tasks.title: Rewrite five technical findings from an examiner's notes into plain wording for a judge, keeping each fact accurate and each claim tied to an exhibit
Work through a seized-laptop fraud image to find the spreadsheet, the deleted emails and the payment records, noting each artefact's location
Complete a fraud investigation from seizure to written report, scored against a rubric on method, accuracy, objectivity and clarity

schedule.title: Evidence law, testimony and ethics
schedule.exercise: Prepare answers to six likely cross-examination questions about your tools, your methods and the limits of your findings.

tasks.title: Judge whether five items of electronic evidence meet authenticity, integrity and relevance tests, and give a reason for each decision
Take part in a mock cross-examination, answering questions on a report and being scored on clarity, honesty and staying within expertise
Handle a case where illegal material turns up during an unrelated search, choosing steps that respect the law, privacy and proportionality

schedule.title: Organisations, incident response and capstone
schedule.exercise: Capstone: write an acceptable-use policy clause and a litigation-hold notice that would let an organisation preserve evidence before an investigation starts.

tasks.title: Place forensic steps at the right stages of an incident response life cycle for a ransomware case and explain what each preserves
Issue a litigation hold for a dispute, list the data sources to preserve, and decide how to handle staff who have already deleted files
Investigate a prepared disk image end to end, produce a report with exhibits and give a mock testimony on your findings
